hints: Focus on what holds molecules together in the liquid, since stronger intermolecular forces mean a higher boiling point.
Sort the four compounds by functional group, two are alkanes, one is a ketone and one is an alcohol.
Remember which type of force allows hydrogen bonding, and think about how much more energy that needs to break compared to other forces.
walkthrough:
**Identify what each compound is**

All four have a similar size with 4 to 5 carbons, so size is not the deciding factor. Let's name them simply.

A is $\text{C(CH}_3)_4$, 2,2-dimethylpropane, a branched alkane. B is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, pentane, a straight-chain alkane. C is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, butan-2-one, a ketone. D is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, butan-2-ol, an alcohol.

**List the strongest intermolecular force in each**

Alkanes A and B are non-polar, so they have only induced dipole-dipole (London) forces. The ketone C is polar due to $\text{C=O}$, so it has permanent dipole-dipole forces plus London forces. The alcohol D has an $\text{-OH}$ group, so it can form hydrogen bonds plus the other forces.

Strength order to remember:
$$\text{London} < \text{dipole-dipole} < \text{hydrogen bonding}$$

**Compare within the same force type**

Between the two alkanes, shape matters. B is long and can pack closely, giving more contact and stronger London forces. A is spherical and branched, giving less surface contact and weaker London forces. So B boils higher than A, but both are still well below polar molecules.

**Pick the winner**

Hydrogen bonding is much stronger than dipole-dipole and London forces, so much more heat energy is needed to separate the molecules into a gas. That makes the alcohol, butan-2-ol, the compound with the highest boiling point.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{C(CH}_3)_4$ is a branched alkane with only weak London forces and a very compact, spherical shape. This gives the smallest surface contact, so it actually has the lowest boiling point of the four.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is straight-chain pentane. It has only London forces, but stronger than A because its long shape gives more contact. It still cannot compete with dipole-dipole or hydrogen bonding.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is a ketone with polar $\text{C=O}$ dipole-dipole forces, so it boils higher than both alkanes. However, it has no $\text{O-H}$ or $\text{N-H}$ bond, so it cannot hydrogen bond to itself and boils lower than an alcohol.
options.D: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is an alcohol with an $\text{-OH}$ group. It forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which are the strongest intermolecular force here and need the most energy to break, giving it the highest boiling point.
